# v061 identifiability (validation only)

This note is the human reading of [identifiability.json](identifiability.json). It uses official valid files only. It is not a test score. It does not edit [docs/v06/](../v06/) or earlier study trees. The dataset is The Well `shear_flow` (CC BY 4).

The oracle is the same weak-form least-squares fit of `nu` and `kappa` as v06, on the clean full field (no lattice, no noise), after periodic Fourier truncation to the listed grid. The v052 center-stride fraction is reused.

A cell passes the identifiability gate when both median relative errors are `<= 0.02`.

## Chosen setting

No swept cell reached the gate for both coefficients on every listed `(Re, Sc)`.

Cheapest CPU-tractable cell on the largest identifiable subset:

- grid `256x512`
- window `late_9` (`frame_start` `160`, `n_frames` `9`, `frame_stride` `1`)
- Reynolds `10000`
- Schmidt values `0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1`
- worst median rel `nu` `0.006580789565276558`
- worst median rel `kappa` `0.002876452178618514`
- `n_combos` `4`
- primary coefficient `kappa`

## What is identifiable

- `nu` cells at the gate: `49` of `208`
- `kappa` cells at the gate: `32` of `208`
- both at the gate: `25` of `208`

No grid or window recovered both coefficients at every listed `(Re, Sc)`. Reynolds values with no passing cell: 50000, 100000, 500000. Kappa is the harder coefficient at high Reynolds and at Schmidt `5`, because the tracer dissipation scale is truncated even on the native grid. Nu is constant on the identifiable Reynolds `10000` slice, so the continuous inverse is kappa.
